Patterns (see Figure 10.1), such as stripes and spots on animal coats or sand ripples on a beach, are very common in nature and in carefully controlled laboratory experiments. They typically occur in systems which are
target_text: Pola (lihat Gambar 10.1), seperti garis dan bintik pada kulit hewan atau riak pasir di pantai, sangat umum dijumpai di alam dan dalam eksperimen laboratorium yang dikendalikan dengan cermat. Pola biasanya muncul dalam sistem yang

source_text: driven far from equilibrium

by external forces or sources of energy. When the forcing is larger than what is necessary to balance inertial forces, the system responds by reorganizing itself into a periodic structure, called a pattern. There are many types of patterns, such as rolls, squares or hexagons, and they can be stationary or dynamic. The study of pattern-forming systems has been the subject of active research in physics, chemistry, nonlinear optics and applied mathematics for more than half a century[footnote]See for instance the book by P. Ball, entitled
target_text: oleh gaya luar atau sumber energi. Ketika gaya penggerak lebih besar daripada yang diperlukan untuk mengimbangi gaya inersia, sistem menanggapinya dengan menata ulang dirinya menjadi struktur periodik yang disebut pola. Ada banyak jenis pola, seperti gulungan, persegi, atau heksagon, dan pola tersebut dapat bersifat stasioner atau dinamis. Kajian tentang sistem pembentuk pola telah menjadi bidang penelitian aktif dalam fisika, kimia, optika nonlinear, dan matematika terapan selama lebih dari setengah abad[footnote]Lihat, misalnya, buku karya P. After finding equilibrium points (stationary and uniform solutions) of this model, the author investigates their linear stability. Figure 2 of the 1999 Klausmeier article shows a level set of the wavelength of the pattern that is expected to grow above threshold, in the $latex (a,m)$ parameter plane, for a fixed value of $latex v$. More precisely, the $latex (a,m)$ plane can be divided into three regions, one where the fixed point corresponding to no vegetation is stable, one where the fixed point corresponding to homogeneous vegetation is stable, and a region in between where linear stability analysis predicts the existence of vegetation patterns. A numerical simulation of the model in this latter regime confirms the existence of traveling stripes on hilly terrain, and of vegetation patches on flat ground. The speed $latex v$ at which water flows downhill measures the steepness of the slope.

source_text: Summary

Different types of patterns may be obtained from the same, generic model, by choosing different sets of parameters. We have seen how to use linear stability analysis to predict whether a pattern can develop from a homogeneous solution as a
target_text: Berbagai jenis pola dapat diperoleh dari model generik yang sama dengan memilih kumpulan parameter yang berbeda. Kita telah melihat cara menggunakan analisis kestabilan linear untuk memprediksi apakah suatu pola dapat berkembang dari solusi homogen ketika sebuah

source_text: control parameter

The orientation of the stripes varies across the picture on the left. Defects (irregularities in the patterns) are visible in both images. Defects present in the stripe pattern include a disclination (looking like an arch), short grain boundaries (lines where stripes with different orientations meet), and dislocations (points where a stripe splits into two). Defect of the hexagonal pattern take the form of penta-hepta pairs (neighboring spots with 5 and 7 neighbors). [
